sourceEvidence.label: EMR4 Bureau architecture, isolation evidence and primary prompt-injection research

assessment.summary: Two structural hardening opportunities should become Gate-zero prerequisites: deterministic information-flow confinement and one-attempt compromise containment for every cognitive cell. This analysis does not implement either control.

nonNegotiables: A provider model participates in every named intelligent dialogue when that capability is available.
Model output remains a non-authoritative candidate.
GraphQL and context frames remain read-only and non-authoritative.
All writes converge on typed REST/OpenAPI commands with backend reauthorization, idempotency, audit and readback.
No model, cognitive cell or proofreader receives database, shell, cloud, deployment or actuator credentials.
Real identity, product-derived data, patient or clinical data, provider runtime, deployment, production and release remain closed.
assumptions: No measured latency, memory or cell-start budget was supplied.
The provider model and local cognitive wrapper can be compromised and can emit deliberately hostile output.
Prompt-injection classifiers, provider safeguards and human review are useful defense in depth but are not authority boundaries.
A later runtime may use OCI containers, microVMs or another isolation platform if it satisfies the same broker contract.

opportunities.title: Confine untrusted influence and protected data with a deterministic Bureau envelope
opportunities.summary: Carry provenance, integrity, confidentiality/readers, freshness and authority ceilings through every value and enforce them at each command and egress sink.
opportunities.diagnosis: The current typed proofreader can reject malformed, stale, ungrounded or unauthorized candidates, but it does not yet prove whether low-integrity data influenced a valid action choice or argument, nor whether every derived value may flow to a proposed recipient.

evidence.claim: The architecture separates cognition, proof, authority and execution and keeps model output non-authoritative.
The threat model requires typed candidates, grounding and authority separation but does not define end-to-end integrity and confidentiality label propagation.
Access AI is the controlled provider route and agent context frames are typed, minimal and non-authoritative.
CaMeL shows that protecting control flow alone does not prevent attacker-controlled tool arguments and proposes provenance-aware capabilities.
FIDES tracks integrity and confidentiality labels and deterministically checks consequential actions and permitted flows.
A schema-valid and grounded candidate can remain attacker-directed unless the proof plane records and enforces the influence of every contributing value.

desiredInvariants: Every source value, transformation, candidate field, command argument and response field has explicit versioned security metadata.
The model cannot create, raise, remove, endorse or declassify any label, reader set, capability or authority claim.
Missing labels and unknown transformations fail closed.
Consequential action selection and every security-relevant argument meet the sink integrity policy.
Every egress destination is permitted by the joined readers of all contributing values.
Confirmation, endorsement and declassification are separate signed, scoped and expiring authority acts.

options.title: Retain schema, grounding and semantic proofreading only
options.summary: Keep the current proof plane without end-to-end influence labels.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Existing typing and grounding remain useful, but they do not expose low-integrity influence over an otherwise valid candidate.

tradeoffs.assessment: Malformed and unsupported drafts still reject, while valid attacker-directed drafts remain possible.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run an injection corpus whose malicious cases preserve schema and cite real facts.

tradeoffs.assessment: No new deterministic checks or data structures enter the path.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Retain the current candidate-to-proofreader latency as the baseline.

tradeoffs.assessment: No label graph or dependency trace is retained.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Record current peak memory for representative typed candidates.

tradeoffs.assessment: The component count stays small, but unsafe influence remains silent rather than producing a typed denial.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Compare failure observability against malicious schema-valid cases.

tradeoffs.assessment: The mental model is familiar, but incident review lacks a source-to-sink influence trace.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Attempt to reconstruct one injected decision from current audit artifacts.

tradeoffs.assessment: No migration is required.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Not applicable beyond preserving existing tests.

residualRisks: A well-formed candidate can encode attacker-selected action choice, parameters or response data.

workPackages: No structural change.
acceptanceCriteria: Not acceptable as the Gate-zero security contract.
migrationNotes: Existing schema and grounding checks remain tactical controls under every other option.

options.title: Freeze an action plan before reading untrusted data
options.summary: Protect action sequence selection and apply deterministic parameter allowlists.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Plan-then-execute gives control-flow integrity but the cited design-pattern analysis records residual argument and content manipulation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Untrusted retrieved data cannot add actions, but it can still redirect allowed arguments and content.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test fixed-plan cases with injected recipient, identifier and free-text fields.

tradeoffs.assessment: A separate plan-freeze step and argument checks add bounded work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50/p95 plan and proof latency against the baseline corpus.

tradeoffs.assessment: One bounded plan and argument trace must survive until completion.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak retained bytes for the largest accepted plan.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fixed workflows are predictable, while legitimate data-dependent branching may reject or encourage overbroad templates.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run representative dialogue tasks and record false-denial and template-expansion rates.

tradeoffs.assessment: Every action family needs a maintained plan template and parameter policy.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory template ownership and simulate a version mismatch.

tradeoffs.assessment: Narrow commands can adopt templates incrementally, but rich Bureau dialogue does not fit one fixed plan.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype one read and one write candidate without widening the plan language.

residualRisks: Attacker-controlled data can still alter allowed arguments, response content or egress payloads.

workPackages: Define fixed plan templates for narrow commands.
Add argument allowlists and injection regression cases.
acceptanceCriteria: Untrusted data cannot add or reorder a tool or command step.
migrationNotes: Use only as defense in depth for commands whose action sequence is truly data-independent.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the template for the affected command and retain schema/grounding checks.

options.title: Propagate security labels and enforce capability policy at every sink
options.summary: Make integrity, confidentiality/readers, provenance, freshness, scope and authority ceilings part of the shared typed Bureau contract.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The option adopts provenance-aware capability checks while retaining direct schema and grounding controls.
The option adapts deterministic integrity and permitted-flow policies to EMR4's existing proof and authority planes.
It fills the observed influence-policy gap without replacing the existing typed command boundary.

tradeoffs.assessment: Low-integrity influence and incompatible reader flows are denied deterministically at each consequential sink.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Use algebraic label tests plus injection cases covering action choice, each argument and each egress field.

tradeoffs.assessment: Typed label joins and sink predicates add bounded CPU and serialization work per value.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50/p95 proof latency and label operations for small, typical and maximum frames; require an explicit Gate-zero budget before runtime selection.

tradeoffs.assessment: A bounded per-request dependency graph and denial trace add retained metadata.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure peak graph bytes and node count at maximum schema bounds; reject unbounded lineage.

tradeoffs.assessment: Missing labels, stale evidence and unknown transforms fail explicitly, although policy or wrapper drift can create safe false denials.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Property-test joins and simulate wrapper/schema version skew, missing metadata and partial outages.

tradeoffs.assessment: A central source/sink registry, policy vocabulary and explainable denial telemetry require ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Exercise policy rollout, rollback, audit reconstruction and an unknown-source incident.

tradeoffs.assessment: Gate zero must freeze the shared envelope before each Bureau wraps its sources and sinks; partial unlabeled operation cannot be permitted.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Build a source/sink inventory and require 100 percent registered coverage before enabling a path.

residualRisks: Incorrect source labels or sink policy can authorize the wrong flow.
Explicitly permitted outputs may retain subtle covert channels.
Provider-side use or retention is outside this local information-flow proof.

workPackages: Freeze label lattice and join rules.
Define trusted wrappers and complete source registry.
Define command/egress sink policies and typed denials.
Define endorsement, declassification and confirmation semantics.
Build property and adversarial acceptance corpus.
acceptanceCriteria: Every admitted value and sink is labeled and registered.
Low-integrity influence cannot trigger a consequential action.
Reader-incompatible data cannot leave through any response or command sink.
migrationNotes: Introduce at Gate zero before any Lane A-D runtime; retain schema, grounding and fixed-plan guards as tactical layers.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Keep all intelligent paths disabled and return to deterministic/manual PMS controls; never fall back to unlabeled model output.

options.title: Add opaque symbolic values to the labeled envelope
options.summary: Hide selected low-integrity or confidential values from the dialogue model and manipulate them through typed handles.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: Symbolic memory and quarantined extraction further reduce model exposure but still require deterministic labels and sink policy.

tradeoffs.assessment: Selected values cannot inject the main dialogue model directly, though quarantined extraction output and reveal policy remain attack surfaces.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test handle substitution, confused-deputy reveals, type smuggling and recipient binding.

tradeoffs.assessment: Quarantined extraction or additional deterministic transforms add calls, copies and policy checks.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure end-to-end latency and provider-call count per workflow against the selected base envelope.

tradeoffs.assessment: A bounded isolated value vault and handle table must live for the request.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure encrypted or isolated value storage and handle-table peak size.

tradeoffs.assessment: Reveal, expiry and handle-resolution failures create more terminal states.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject stale, missing, duplicated and cross-request handles.

tradeoffs.assessment: Debugging becomes harder because operators should not inspect protected values casually.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Design a privacy-preserving incident trace and rehearse one failed reveal.

tradeoffs.assessment: Only workflows that can express protected values symbolically can adopt it without losing dialogue utility.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype one high-risk field after the base envelope passes and measure task completion.

residualRisks: Reveal policy can become a confused deputy.
Many legitimate explanations require deliberate access to the hidden value.

workPackages: Select eligible field classes.
Define opaque handles and expiry.
Define extraction and reveal schemas.
Add cross-handle and covert-output tests.
acceptanceCriteria: The main dialogue model cannot dereference protected handles.
Only a permitted sink resolves a handle after label policy passes.
migrationNotes: Defer until the selected base envelope is stable; add per field rather than replacing the shared contract.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable symbolic handling for the affected workflow and keep that intelligent path closed until the base labeled path is safe.

opportunities.recommendation: Adopt the labeled capability envelope as a Gate-zero prerequisite. Retain fixed plans as a narrow supplementary guard and consider symbolic values later for fields whose exposure is both high risk and unnecessary for dialogue.

opportunities.title: Contain a compromised cognitive wrapper and eliminate ambient host bridges
opportunities.summary: Run each Bureau attempt in a fresh broker-mediated cell with one typed input, one typed output and no ambient authority surface.
opportunities.diagnosis: EMR4 has bounded isolation evidence, but the future model runtime lacks a frozen complete bridge inventory and one-attempt lifetime contract. A later parser, file, URL, callback, telemetry or generic tool convenience could therefore convert hostile model output into host compromise or cross-Bureau persistence.

evidence.claim: The earlier rehearsal used a pinned non-root, read-only, mount-free and network-free container profile.
The earlier evidence explicitly did not prove host-kernel, daemon, prompt/tool or adaptive-model safety.
Agent admission starts with empty tools, secrets and capabilities and permits draft-only egress.
Microsoft documented model-controlled input reaching evaluation and host file-write bridges in agent frameworks.
If a future cognitive wrapper exposes any unregistered host bridge, compromise before proofreading can bypass the intended typed-candidate boundary.

desiredInvariants: Each Bureau attempt has a fresh cell generation, identity, quotas and empty writable state.
The model-accessible surface is exactly one closed typed input and one closed candidate output.
Provider transport, credentials, destinations, retry and budgets remain broker-owned and immutable to the model.
The cell has no ambient shell, code, tool, filesystem, host path, socket, metadata, database, cloud or actuator capability.
The broker treats model output as hostile bytes and never evaluates or dereferences model-selected code, objects, paths, URLs or callbacks.
Every bridge is registered, policy-bound, auditable and denied when unknown.
Every terminal state destroys the cell and produces bounded residue evidence.

options.title: Use one long-lived hardened container for all Bureaus
options.summary: Keep a warm shared runtime with ordinary container hardening and network policy.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The existing profile reduces privilege but does not remove cross-request lifetime, shared state or future bridge accumulation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Non-root, read-only and capability restrictions narrow compromise, while one breach can persist across attempts and Bureaus.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Test cross-request memory, filesystem, cache and process residue after a simulated compromise.

tradeoffs.assessment: A warm runtime avoids per-attempt startup and image initialization.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure warm request latency as the baseline for later isolation options.

tradeoffs.assessment: One shared process can reuse model-client and parser memory.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure steady-state RSS and cache growth under a representative concurrent workload.

tradeoffs.assessment: Warm caches reduce startup failures, but persistent corruption can affect later unrelated requests.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject parser and process corruption and observe subsequent attempts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Fewer runtime objects simplify ordinary operation, but incident scope and residue analysis are broader.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse containment and attribution of one compromised request.

tradeoffs.assessment: It most closely resembles a conventional service and needs the least orchestration work.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Inventory all required bridges and compare them to the desired empty-capability contract.

residualRisks: Compromise and writable state can span attempts.
A shared runtime can recreate cross-Bureau memory or capability paths.

workPackages: Apply conventional container hardening.
acceptanceCriteria: Not acceptable as the shared Gate-zero lifetime contract.
migrationNotes: The same hardening flags remain required under disposable options.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Stop the shared runtime and keep intelligent paths disabled.

options.title: Create one sealed brokered cell per Bureau attempt
options.summary: Give one fresh cell one typed request and one candidate response while a deterministic broker owns provider transport and every external sink.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: The option promotes proven isolation properties into a future runtime contract and adds per-attempt lifetime and bridge completeness.
Removing model-accessible evaluation, host paths and generic tools blocks the documented structural bridge classes.
The broker contract applies least privilege, temporary identity, scope, monitoring and incident-ready receipts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Compromise is bounded to one attempt with no ambient host, network, credential or cross-Bureau bridge; the broker remains a new high-trust parser and transport component.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Run bridge, parser-smuggling, metadata, socket, file, credential, cross-Bureau and residue attacks against the chosen runtime.

tradeoffs.assessment: Cell creation, input copy, provider relay and teardown add hops and cold-start latency.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure p50/p95/p99 creation-to-teardown latency for the maximum approved concurrent workload and set an explicit Gate-zero threshold.

tradeoffs.assessment: Concurrent attempts require separate bounded processes and buffers, though nothing persists after teardown.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure per-cell and broker peak RSS at the selected concurrency and reject unbounded queues.

tradeoffs.assessment: A failed cell cannot corrupt the next attempt; broker, startup and teardown add explicit failure modes that must fail closed.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject provider timeout, malformed output, quota kill, broker restart and teardown failure and verify typed terminal receipts.

tradeoffs.assessment: Pinned images, runtime profiles, bridge registry, quotas and residue monitoring need clear ownership.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Rehearse image revocation, bridge-version mismatch, quota alert and compromised-cell investigation.

tradeoffs.assessment: Gate zero must define a platform-neutral broker contract, followed by a provider-free runtime proof before any occupied model call.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Build a source-hashed runtime manifest and prove zero unregistered bridges before enabling an occupied rehearsal.

residualRisks: Unknown host, kernel or container-runtime vulnerabilities can escape the cell.
The broker parser or provider relay can contain implementation defects.
Provider-side compromise remains outside the cell boundary.

workPackages: Freeze one-attempt input/output contract.
Freeze broker-owned provider envelope and immutable binding.
Define runtime and parser admission profile.
Define bridge registry, quotas, teardown and residue schemas.
Build provider-free adversarial runtime acceptance.
acceptanceCriteria: The cell has no ambient authority or cross-attempt state.
Malformed or hostile output reaches no interpreter or sink.
Every terminal state destroys the cell and records residue.
migrationNotes: Keep all intelligent paths default-off until a concrete runtime proves the contract; use pre-pulled pinned layers only if they preserve isolation.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Disable the affected intelligent path, revoke its broker binding and return to deterministic/manual PMS controls.

options.title: Place each one-shot cell behind a separate kernel
options.summary: Use the same broker contract with a disposable microVM or comparable hardware-isolated runtime.

evidenceCoverage.rationale: A separate kernel further narrows container escape while preserving the same no-bridge and hostile-output controls.

tradeoffs.assessment: A separate kernel narrows shared-kernel escape paths but does not remove broker, hypervisor, provider or policy risk.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Review the chosen microVM threat model and run the same bridge and residue suite plus hypervisor-specific tests.

tradeoffs.assessment: Boot, device setup and teardown are likely slower than a disposable container.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Benchmark p50/p95/p99 end-to-end latency against one-shot containers on the actual host.

tradeoffs.assessment: Each concurrent attempt carries a guest-kernel and fixed runtime footprint.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Measure resident memory and maximum safe concurrency on the target infrastructure.

tradeoffs.assessment: Failure isolation improves while more orchestration and boot components create new failure modes.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Fault-inject image, boot, relay, teardown and capacity failures.

tradeoffs.assessment: Kernel images, hypervisor patching, capacity, telemetry and incident response require a mature platform owner.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Produce an ownership and patch-SLA rehearsal before selection.

tradeoffs.assessment: The stable broker protocol makes runtime replacement possible, but no current platform evidence establishes the practical cost.
tradeoffs.validationPlan: Prototype the same frozen broker test suite on one candidate microVM runtime.

residualRisks: Higher latency or resource pressure may make the intelligent path unavailable.
It does not change authority or information-flow policy.

affectedComponents: Runtime implementation beneath the broker contract
workPackages: Select a supported microVM platform.
Benchmark resource and reliability behavior.
Re-run all one-shot cell security acceptance.
acceptanceCriteria: It passes the unchanged broker contract and improves the agreed isolation property within an accepted latency and capacity budget.
migrationNotes: Defer until measurements or a high-risk runtime justify separate-kernel isolation; keep the broker protocol interchangeable.
implementationReadiness.rollback: Return to a previously accepted one-shot runtime profile without changing labels, provider binding or authority semantics.

opportunities.recommendation: Adopt the platform-neutral one-shot brokered cell as the Gate-zero minimum. Preserve microVM isolation as a compatible stronger profile if later measurements or recovery-domain risk justify its operating cost.

openQuestions: What p95 latency and concurrent-cell memory budgets should Gate zero impose before selecting a concrete runtime?
Which response fields, if any, justify the deferred symbolic-vault extension?
Which platform control will enforce outbound provider allowlisting without exposing a general HTTP client to the cell?
What authorized human roles may endorse or declassify each future data class?
